name: v0.1.0 preview
body:
BlahDNS Browser Extension 0.1.0 is a manual-install privacy extension preview for Chrome, Brave, and Firefox.

It uses browser-native Manifest V3 DNR filtering, with 100,619 distinct bundled ad, tracker, and content-farm domains compiled into 225 default rules. It includes domain-tree scopes and exceptions, supported hosts/ABP and cosmetic rules, HTTPS subscriptions, tracking-parameter cleanup, settings import/export, and local opt-in aggregate counters.

Native controls include WebRTC policies, advanced HTTP User-Agent and en-US headers, Firefox native fingerprint resistance, and destination-scoped HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS proxy configuration. SG and DE BlahDNS endpoints have manual DoH setup instructions and a POST diagnostic.

Validation: 36 unit tests pass. Chrome and Brave each pass 14 integration checks. Firefox passes 15. The browser suite covers real request and WebSocket blocking, strict-CSP cosmetic filtering, settings UI, import/export payloads, native policy read-back, scopes, HTTP proxy routing, and SOCKS5 remote DNS. Both live DNS diagnostics return NOERROR. Source notices, security corrections, benchmark results, and limitations are in docs/evals/.

Installation:

- Extract the Chromium ZIP. In Chrome or Brave, open chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, choose Load unpacked, and select the extracted folder containing manifest.json.
- Extract the Firefox ZIP. In about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox, choose Load Temporary Add-on and select manifest.json. Firefox removes a temporary add-on at restart. Permanent installation requires a signed XPI.
- Check each archive against SHA256SUMS.

Limits: DoH setup is manual. Native WebRTC and Firefox RFP are browser-wide. UA and language changes affect HTTP headers only. The extension does not inject canvas/audio/WebGL noise or guarantee CAPTCHA acceptance. HTTP/2, HTTP/3, QUIC, and UDP coverage remain browser/network behavior. HTTPS proxy TLS, SOCKS4 end-to-end traffic, native permission dialogs, minimum browser versions, and specific fingerprint surfaces are not fully covered by this test matrix. GitHub packages are not signed browser-store releases.

Privacy: no telemetry, cloud sync, remote code, or stored browsing history. Runtime dependencies: none. Development uses mise-managed Bun and its native tools.
